clue.text: Patient wearing undies must get bags

indicators.note: the undies have the patient inside them, as clothes are worn around a body

parts.note: briefs are underpants
a doctor's patient is a case

explanation.surface: A hospital patient in only their underwear is told to fetch their luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: Briefcases are flat bags for carrying papers, so they are a kind of bag.

clue.text: British student with German bloke getting drunk

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car
Otto is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: A British student and a German man get drunk together.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is British slang for very drunk.

clue.text: Arrival of popular fellow with light unit

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
the lux is the SI unit of illumination

explanation.surface: A well-liked man turns up carrying a lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: An influx is an arrival of many people or things, a flowing in.

clue.text: Hatters top — form exceptional, mainly

indicators.note: exceptional means out of the ordinary, so these letters break out of their normal order

explanation.surface: A sports report: the Hatters, top of the league, in exceptional form.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hatters is the nickname of Luton Town football club.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning largely or in most cases, which is mainly.

clue.text: A couple of roads up at home? This causes an increase in blood pressure

definitions.text: This causes an increase in blood pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pair of roads is read from bottom to top

parts.note: two kinds of road: a lane, and RD, the abbreviation for road
two kinds of road: a lane, and RD, the abbreviation for road
in means at home

explanation.surface: Two roads uphill to the house would raise anyone's blood pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A couple of roads' looks like one unit, but the A stands apart and the couple gives LANE and RD; turned 'up' they make DRENAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The hormone released by the adrenal glands raises heart rate and blood pressure in stress.

clue.text: Vote in European swindle for one who's served his time

indicators.note: the voting mark goes in, between the other two pieces

parts.note: a con is a swindle
X is the cross marked on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A vote in a European scam benefits a released prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: A former convict has finished a prison sentence, served his time.

clue.text: Voices disapproval of nameless benefits

indicators.note: without a name, so the letter N, short for name, is dropped

parts.note: boons are benefits or blessings

explanation.surface: Someone complains loudly about anonymous welfare payments.
explanation.definitionFit: To boo is to jeer, voicing disapproval of a performer or speaker.

clue.text: Make repairs to complete catch

parts.note: over means finished, complete
a haul is a catch, as of fish

explanation.surface: A boat needs fixing to land a full catch.
explanation.definitionFit: To overhaul a machine is to strip it down and repair it.

clue.text: Put the accent on tense

definitions.meaning: to emphasise a syllable or word

explanation.surface: Emphasising a verb tense in a grammar lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A stressed syllable carries the accent, and a stressed person is tense and anxious.

clue.text: Funding from seat of government supporting undertaking

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits below the first, holding it up

parts.note: a venture is a risky undertaking
a capital city is where government sits

explanation.surface: Money from the capital city backs a new project.
explanation.definitionFit: Venture capital is money invested in new businesses, a form of funding.

clue.text: Not at work — ears oddly tender!

parts.note: someone off is not at work

indicators.note: taking the odd-numbered letters of the word ears, first and third

explanation.surface: Someone off work complains their ears are sore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' looks like the adjective 'sore', but it is the verb or noun: to tender is to put forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To tender a bid or resignation is to present it, a synonym of putting it forward.

clue.text: Awful noise, always ignoring volume — that's criminal

parts.note: a racket is a din

indicators.note: the word for always leaves out, ignores, the letter for volume

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: Complaining that a constant din at full volume is a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer runs a dishonest racket, so is a kind of criminal, typically in organised crime.

clue.text: Season — time enough possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the word enough can be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A cook judges whether a seasoning time is long enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Season' suggests flavouring food, but here it means to harden, as timber is seasoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasoning wood or a person means hardening it through exposure, which is making it tougher.

clue.text: Memos about church scores

indicators.note: the memos go about, surrounding, the church abbreviation

parts.note: notes are short memos

explanation.surface: Office notes concerning a church tally up the results.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is a notch or cut made as a tally mark, so notches are scores.

clue.text: Surprisingly, most earn full amount

indicators.note: the letters of these three words come out in a surprising new order

explanation.surface: A surprising report that most people are paid the full sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full amount' reads as one phrase, but 'full' belongs to the fodder; only 'amount' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fortune is an idiom for a large sum of money, an amount.

clue.text: Craft of boxer holding on

indicators.note: the boxer holds the word for on inside his grip

parts.note: a boxer is a fighter
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A boxer's skill lies in clinging on in a clinch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' reads as skill, but means a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A freighter is a cargo ship, a seagoing craft.

clue.text: Quiet doctor surrounded by fat people suddenly gathering

indicators.note: the quiet and doctor pieces sit inside the word for fat

parts.note: flab is body fat
sh is a call for quiet
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A discreet doctor finds himself hemmed in by overweight patients crowding round.
explanation.definitionFit: A flash mob is a group that assembles suddenly in public, performs, then disperses.

clue.text: On holiday, finished revealing hurt feelings

parts.note: someone off is away from work on holiday
ended means finished

explanation.surface: A holiday comes to an end, and someone's feelings are wounded.
explanation.definitionFit: To be offended is to have hurt feelings, insulted or upset.

clue.text: Time for a few words about oneself?

definitions.text: Time for a few words about oneself?

parts.words: Time for a few words about oneself?
parts.note: 'time' is prison time, and the phrase also reads as a sentence about one's own life, an autobiography in brief

explanation.surface: Asking whether it is the moment to say a little about yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprisonment for life is a lengthy term of time served, and the words also suggest a one-line biography.

clue.text: Put down limits of damage, on average

indicators.note: the limits are the outer letters, first and last, of the word damage

parts.note: the mean is the average

explanation.surface: An insurer belittles the bounds of damage by averaging it out.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to belittle or humiliate them, to put them down.

clue.text: Resources needed by group on board a ship

indicators.note: the group is on board, inside the steamship

parts.note: SS is a steamship
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A list of supplies a crew needs aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets are things of value a person or firm owns, their resources.

clue.text: Measures should incorporate exercises in areas of Russia

indicators.note: the measures take the exercises into their body, enclosing them

parts.note: steps are measures taken to an end
PE is physical education, exercises

explanation.surface: Instructions that a fitness plan should include workouts across Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: The steppes are vast grassland plains of Russia and Central Asia.

clue.text: Sun king runs in it to go around

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for Sunday
K is king in chess and cards

indicators.note: the runs letter is placed in the word it

parts.note: R is runs in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A Sun King runs about in circles.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun King was Louis XIV of France, but here the words split into separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To skirt something is to pass round its edge rather than through it.

clue.text: Good horse getting agitated around quiet rodents

indicators.note: the rearranged horse wraps round the musical letter for quiet
agitated letters are stirred up and rearranged

parts.note: P is piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: A good horse grows restless around silent burrowing animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Gophers are North American burrowing rodents with cheek pouches.

clue.text: Avant-garde artist stormed in drunk

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so these letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A bohemian painter bursts into the room drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A modernist broke with tradition in art, an avant-garde practitioner.

clue.text: Subject of note crossing border

indicators.note: the note spans across the border, with the border inside it

parts.note: TE is a note of the sol-fa scale, also written ti
a hem is the border of cloth

explanation.surface: The topic of a musical note running over a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the topic or subject of a talk or piece of writing.

clue.text: Girl getting married has no right to wait

indicators.note: the bride lacks the letter standing for right

parts.note: a bride is a woman on her wedding day

explanation.surface: A girl about to wed has no right to make anyone wait.
explanation.definitionFit: To bide, as in 'bide your time', means to wait patiently.

clue.text: Plots succeeded initially with Conservative approaches

indicators.note: taking only the opening letter of the word succeeded

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
lines are approaches, as in lines of attack or argument

explanation.surface: Schemes that worked at first once the Tories had their angles.
explanation.definitionFit: Storylines are the plots of novels, films or dramas.
